common_errors: Swapping sine and cosine between the x and y components.
Using the wrong angle reference axis when assigning sine and cosine.
Ignoring quadrant signs and assigning the wrong sign to a component.
Treating the vector magnitude as a single component value.
Omitting units on component or vector answers.
Using degrees and radians inconsistently when evaluating trigonometric functions.
Reporting only the magnitude instead of both rectangular components.
procedure.concept: A 2D vector can be represented by perpendicular components along the coordinate axes. The component aligned with the angle reference uses cosine when the angle is measured from that axis; the perpendicular component uses sine. Component signs must follow the vector's actual quadrant and the chosen positive axes.

failure_signal_mappings.trigger_condition: Wrong angle reference, sine/cosine swap, or incorrect adjacent-vs-opposite component assignment.
Incorrect component signs or quadrant direction relative to the stated axes.
Unit omission, incomplete vector notation, or magnitude check failure.

formula.notation: If θ is measured counterclockwise from +x: F_x = F cos(θ), F_y = F sin(θ). Vector form: F = F_x i + F_y j. Magnitude check: |F| = sqrt(F_x^2 + F_y^2). If θ is measured from the y-axis or another reference axis, identify the adjacent and opposite components before assigning sine and cosine.

procedure: Draw or identify the vector and the coordinate axes, including the positive x and y directions.
Identify the angle reference axis and the quadrant in which the vector lies.
Determine which component is adjacent to the given angle and which is opposite (cosine for adjacent, sine for opposite when θ is measured from the reference axis).
Compute the component magnitudes using sine and cosine with the given magnitude and angle.
Assign signs to F_x and F_y based on the vector direction and the axis convention.
Write the vector in component form with units (F = F_x i + F_y j).
Check the result by recomputing the magnitude and verifying the direction sense.

worked_example.prompt: A 500 N force acts 30 degrees above the positive x-axis. Resolve the force into x and y components and write it in vector form. Use standard x-y axes (+x right, +y up), with the angle measured counterclockwise from +x. Units: newtons.
solution_steps: Draw the force at 30° above +x in the first quadrant; axes: +x right, +y up; angle reference: CCW from +x.
Angle reference axis is +x; the vector lies in the first quadrant (both components positive).
F_x is adjacent to θ (uses cosine); F_y is opposite (uses sine).
Both components are positive in the first quadrant: F_x = +433 N, F_y = +250 N.
Magnitude check: sqrt(433^2 + 250^2) = sqrt(187489 + 62500) ≈ 500 N, matching the given magnitude.
